key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source platform for excited-state materials simulations that avoids explicit virtual states while supporting GW, BSE, TDDFT, and related workflows.
engineering_relevance: For solar-cell and optoelectronic materials design, WEST enables predictive excited-state calculations on large, complex systems with GPU-accelerated performance.
method: Full-frequency GW, Bethe-Salpeter equation, and TDDFT in one framework
Density-functional and density-matrix perturbation theory with low-rank screening/exchange
Hierarchical parallelization plus GPU acceleration for near-ideal strong scaling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports representative applications across spin defects, self-trapped excitons in metal-halide perovskites, and water/ice, with scaling to systems of more than a thousand atoms.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on advanced parallel/GPU infrastructure and on the underlying approximations used to avoid explicit virtual-state calculations.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
